name: South Brazil (Paraná · Santa Catarina · Rio Grande do Sul)

language.script_notes: Some German (Hunsrückisch) and Italian (Talian) village and business names survive in the colonial highland towns, alongside standard Portuguese signage.

road_furniture.bollard_color: No standard bollard, as elsewhere in Brazil.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam; concrete barrier on the main highways (BR-101, BR-116, Free Way).
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; tidy, well-kept streetscapes compared with much of Brazil.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The national ladder-and-holes concrete pole. Roads and farms are noticeably more orderly and better-maintained than the national average.

architecture.roof_style: Steeper pitched roofs than the rest of Brazil, reflecting the cooler, wetter climate.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile and painted sheet metal.
architecture.wall_construction: Masonry, plus timber and half-timbered (enxaimel / Fachwerk) construction in the German-settled areas.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White with dark timber framing in the colonial towns; also brick and pastel render.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: German half-timbered houses and churches (Pomerode, Blumenau, Gramado), Italian stone houses and wineries in the Serra Gaúcha, and orderly European-style farmsteads. No hillside favelas.

nature.vegetation: Araucaria (Paraná pine) — flat-topped, umbrella-shaped conifers — across the highlands is the signature. Atlantic Forest on the coast; open Pampa grassland across most of Rio Grande do Sul.
nature.terrain: Rolling highland plateau and the Serra Geral escarpment (deep canyons such as Itaimbezinho), a narrow coastal plain, and flat grassland toward the Uruguayan border.
nature.climate_signature: The coolest part of Brazil — four distinct seasons, winter frost on the highlands, and rare light snow at the highest points. Light is often lower and greyer than the tropical north.

vehicles.plate_color: Mercosur white plate with a blue 'BRASIL' strip; older grey plates common; red commercial plates.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: National mix. More agricultural machinery and cattle transport in the Pampa; gaúcho ranching culture.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good, dense coverage across all three states, mostly white car. Winter scenes can look distinctly un-tropical — bare trees, frost, grey skies.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The Pampa grassland in Rio Grande do Sul is nearly identical to Uruguay — flat pasture, cattle, big skies
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Language is the tell: Portuguese vs Spanish. Brazil keeps its Mercosur 'BRASIL' plates and ladder-and-holes concrete poles; Uruguay's signage, plates and poles differ.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Pampa landscape, cattle country, right-hand drive
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Portuguese vs Spanish signage; Brazilian plates and poles; and the araucaria highlands and German/Italian towns have no Argentine equivalent this far south.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country furniture, language and Atlantic Forest coast
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The South is cooler with araucaria pines, half-timbered European architecture, steeper roofs and no favelas; the Southeast is hot, has hillside favelas and much larger cities.
